(Fetched via WebFetch text extraction — condensed by fetch tool; direct curl blocked. Times of Israel newsroom. By Agencies and ToI Staff, October 17, 2026, 4:01 pm Israel time)
Admiral Brad Cooper, head of US Central Command, stated in a video message that "there are reports" indicating Tehran's regional proxies were withholding fighter payments to "funnel money back" to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

Cooper announced the US had blocked $25 billion in Iranian crude oil exports and frozen $35 million in Iranian cryptocurrency. He assessed that "The Islamic regime is clearly feeling the economic pain" as a consequence of these measures.

The admiral also claimed the "Strait of Hormuz is controlled by the United States and our regional partners, not Iran," despite reports of at least one tanker being struck in the waterway.

The IRGC stated that an oil tanker caught fire after hitting a mine while attempting to transit the strait with disabled tracking systems. The statement described the vessel as carrying over two million barrels and characterized its passage as "illegal."

UK Maritime Trade Operations reported a separate tanker struck by an "unknown projectile" off Saudi Arabia's coast, with all crew reported safe. A second vessel was reportedly attacked by rocket-propelled grenade in the same area.

According to Wall Street Journal sources, increased Iranian military assistance has enabled Yemen's Houthi rebels to gain ground against Saudi-backed forces. Sources indicated IRGC officers were present on frontlines directing attacks using advanced drone technology.
